category_title: Middle school students with severe reading disabilities who disengage from traditional tasks
student_description: This 13-year-old student has severe reading disabilities that cause him to become passive, 'invisible,' and frustrated during traditional pen-to-paper tasks. He uniquely requires age-appropriate digital tools with multimodal options (images, audio, text prediction) to bypass writing barriers, alongside tight timelines and peer-sharing to motivate him.

criteria.rationale: Traditional pen-to-paper tasks cause this student to become frustrated and 'invisible,' so writing barriers must be bypassed using digital, visual tools.
criteria.check: The tutor assigns or adapts tasks to use digital, multimodal tools (e.g., mind-mapping, images, digital apps) rather than traditional pen-to-paper methods.

criteria.rationale: This student tends to quietly search the internet for off-task items and needs immediate boundaries to realize he cannot get away with it.
criteria.check: If the student exhibits off-task behavior (e.g., internet browsing), the tutor immediately redirects them to the task and explicitly emphasizes the need to stay focused.

criteria.rationale: Providing simple walk-through guides allows this student to independently solve problems rather than giving up and putting his head down.
criteria.check: The tutor provides or references a simple, step-by-step 'walk-through guide' or reference tool to help the student independently troubleshoot issues.

criteria.rationale: As a 13-year-old, using materials designed for younger students causes him to disengage, so content must respect his actual age.
criteria.check: The tutor ensures that the suggested tools, reading materials, or programs are age-appropriate for a middle-school student and explicitly avoids 'babyish' or primary-level resources.
